task:
Fix two layout problems on the home page found when the merged home page (PR #1013, `apps/web/src/routes/+page.svelte`) was viewed in a real browser. Start from current main. apps/web only; do not touch assets/, PROVENANCE.json, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, the images, other routes, the API or any file under src/lib/features/explore/ (import only). No new dependencies, no new colour literals (kit tokens only).

PROBLEM 1 — the reference-system search box is too narrow on desktop. With the Finder archetype UI on (the release build, `VITE_FINDER_F4_ENABLED=1`), the form puts reference system, archetype and the button in one row inside the 46%-wide copy column, so at 1280x800 the input is only about 188 px wide and its placeholder is cut off ("Try Sol, Achenar, La"); at 1024x768 it is about 207 px. FIX: lay the form out as two rows on desktop: row 1 the Reference system field at full column width; row 2 the Colony archetype select and the orange "Find a system →" button side by side (button keeps its size, select takes the rest). When the archetype UI is off (flag 0) keep one row: the input fills the width and the button sits beside it. Phones (<= 640px) keep the current stacked layout (input, select, full-width button). The error message row and focus behaviour stay as they are. Acceptance (measured in Cypress with F4 on): reference input width >= 320 px at 1280x800, >= 280 px at 1024x768, and the full placeholder "Try Sol, Achenar, Lave…" fits without truncation at both; at 390x844 the input is full width as today.

PROBLEM 2 — on phones the black hole background is effectively invisible. At <= 640 px wide the dark scrim over the hero is about 94% opaque everywhere, so the owner's black hole screenshot shows only as a faint smudge. The owner wants the black hole to be the home background on every screen size. FIX for <= 640 px only (desktop composition stays exactly as is): make the hero a stacked layout where the image is a visible band at the TOP of the hero and the copy sits below it on the solid page background. The band is the 960 px image, object-fit cover, centred so the black hole ring stays in view, height clamp(14rem, 36svh, 20rem), with only a bottom fade into --bg-void (a token-only linear-gradient over the last ~35% of the band) and NO scrim over the visible part. The copy (eyebrow, h1, lede, form, notes) starts below the band on --bg-void, so text contrast is trivially AA there. Keep the image decorative (aria-hidden, alt=""), keep reserved size (no layout shift), no animation. Do not preload extra images. Tablet widths (641-1023 px) must keep working: check 768x1024 and make sure the image is visible and the text stays AA readable (use the stacked band layout up to 900 px if the side-by-side composition cannot keep the copy off the bright part of the image).

TESTS AND EVIDENCE
- Update apps/web/src/routes/page.test.ts only if it pins the changed markup/classes; add component or CSS-contract tests where the repo already has that pattern.
- Cypress product-journey: add layout assertions for the measurements above (input widths at 1280x800 and 1024x768; at 390x844 the hero image's bounding box top is within the first 40 percent of the viewport height, its rendered height is >= 14rem, and the h1 starts below the image band; no horizontal overflow at 1280, 1024, 768 and 390). Keep the existing home-to-Explore journey test. Save screenshots product/home-hero-desktop, product/home-hero-laptop (1024x768), product/home-hero-tablet (768x1024) and product/home-hero-phone with fullPage capture so the whole page is visible (the existing screenshots are cropped at the test window height).
- Run pnpm check, pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm test, pnpm build in apps/web (pnpm 11.25.0).
- Update the contrast figures in the CHANGES entry for the changed phone layout (the phone copy now sits on --bg-void; state the computed ratios for --text, --text-muted and --accent against --bg-void).

CHANGES.md: add a new top entry with the exact heading `## 2026-11-04 — UI redesign: home page layout fixes` explaining in plain words what the owner will see: a wider search box on desktop and the black hole now clearly visible on phones. Do not edit the existing home entries.
